For a Colorado family of four with a stable thyroid condition and young kids, here's my recommendation:

**Go with a Silver ACA marketplace plan (Connect for Health Colorado) — best balance of predictability and cost.**

**Why Silver:**
• Cost-sharing reductions (CSR) kick in at 200–250% FPL (~$60k–$75k for family of 4), lowering deductibles/co-pays significantly
• Thyroid generic (levothyroxine) is Tier 1 on all formularies — $0–$5 copay
• Pediatric visits: $0 copay for well-child (ACA preventive mandate)
• Predictable: $20–$40 specialist copays, $10–$20 urgent care, $250–$500 ER

**Top carriers in CO (2024):**
• Kaiser Permanente Silver 70 HMO — integrated system, own labs/pharmacy, $0 generic, $30 specialist, ~$1,400/mo family premium before subsidy
• Cigna Silver 70 EPO — broader network, $5 generic, $40 specialist, ~$1,550/mo
• Anthem Silver 70 PPO — largest network, $10 generic, $50 specialist, ~$1,650/mo

**If income > 400% FPL (no subsidy):** consider Gold HMO (~$1,800/mo) for lower deductible ($500 vs $3,500) and $15 specialist.

**Avoid:** Bronze (high deductible = unpredictable), HDHP/HSA (thyroid labs + kid visits = hit deductible fast), short-term plans (no pre-existing coverage).
